interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors. Positive prognostic indicators include negative surgical margins, absence of seminal vesicle invasion, and no lymph node metastasis reported in the prostatectomy specimen. These findings suggest a favorable local disease course. The preoperative PSA was 4.8 ng/mL, which contributes to the risk assessment. A countervailing finding is the pathological Gleason score of 4+4 (ISUP grade group 4) from the surgical specimen, indicating high-grade cancer. Furthermore, the biopsy showed Gleason 4+4 in the right side with a cribriform pattern, consistent with the higher grade seen post-surgery. The nodal status was assessed and reported as negative for metastasis. Prognosis revision would be significantly aided by postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory over time. The fixed estimated horizon is 69.39 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 55.52–83.27 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 4.8 and an ISUP grade group 4 identified both at biopsy and post-prostatectomy. Favorable findings include negative surgical margins, no seminal vesicle invasion, absence of lymphovascular invasion, and no documented lymph node metastasis. The pathological T stage was pT2, which is favorable. Biopsy findings were consistent with the prostatectomy specimen regarding high grade (Gleason 4+4). Missing postoperative PSA data prevents a more refined assessment of current disease status. Future prognosis would be significantly revised by obtaining postoperative PSA levels and tracking their subsequent trajectory over time. The documented nodal sampling provides information, and no uncertainty exists regarding node status based on the provided records.
